title: A bounded flat model of finite Tor amplitude
statement: Let $C$ be a braided closed monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor is additive in each variable, with functorial flat resolutions and a chosen derived category $D(C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Equip $D(C)$ with the K-flat derived tensor product. An object of $C$ is flat when tensoring with it is exact. For $K\in D(C)$ and integers $a,b$, say that $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ when $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F[0])=0$ for every $F\in C$ and every $i<a$ or $b<i$. Then any such $K$ is isomorphic to $Q(S)$ for a complex $S$ of flat objects with $S^i=0$ for $i<a$ or $b<i$.

source.place: DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_flat_of_torAmplitudeIn; bounded flat model and derived tensor bounds, cf. Stacks Tags 0654 and 06Y7

proof.text: Test the amplitude on the tensor unit to bound K. Choose a bounded-above flat resolution vanishing above b. Its good truncation below a still represents K. The term in degree a is the opcycles of the resolution; the Tor test in degree a-1 makes that opcycles object flat by the categorical Tor criterion. All remaining terms are flat or zero. This is the already proved generic source theorem, read at FlatModel.lean:260-297.
